comments.author: @Canadian-l3y
comments.text: My Dad, a businessman, took his family to Temagami, Ontario, where he and Mom built a log cabin from scratch out of the surrounding forest. No radios, let alone TV; no electricity; no running water; bears, trees, and 4-billion-year-old rocks for company; and winters reaching 40 below. Best childhood a kid could dream of!

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: What an incredible childhood story. Growing up in a hand-built log cabin surrounded by forests, wildlife, ancient rock, and real northern winters must have created memories that stay with you for a lifetime. It sounds simple by modern standards, but also incredibly rich in experience, freedom, and connection to nature. Thank you for sharing such a special piece of your family history with us.

comments.author: @herbtarlic892
comments.text: I'm a 77yr old Canadian living in Toronto, on the shores of beautiful Lake ONTARIO, which was carved out of the Canadian Shield rock, by 5 mile thick glaciers as they pushed south into the U.S. I have been to many of those places you have showcased in your video and I can tell you that your description of them is accurate in every detail. I had to chuckle at your description of our fondness for maple syrup and our propensity for apologizing, and tacking "eh" onto every sentence. That's just who we are, eh! Generally, we're a quiet people in a quiet country and we like it that way. Although, given the current arc of 21st century history, we've had to be a little less quiet. Don't you worry, we'll get this sorted and keep our land glorious and free. Thanks for a great video, eh!

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: What a wonderful comment! Hearing this from a 77-year-old Canadian who has personally visited so many of the places featured in our film means a great deal to us. We're especially happy that our little observations about maple syrup, apologies, and the famous Canadian "eh" made you chuckle! Your words reflect such a deep connection to your homeland. We hope Canada continues to preserve the natural beauty, peaceful communities, and traditions you cherish. Thank you for sharing your experience and for making this comment section even more special. Wishing you good health and many more beautiful years by Lake Ontario. Take care, eh! ❤🇨🇦
